comment:
The course was designed for music majors, not for average students who just want a gen ed credit so if you are the latter, just keep away from her. Very little room for mistakes. Make a minor mistake and prepare to fall down a grade. 
Oh did I mention extra work? Be prepared for MANDATORY OUT-OF-CLASS LECTURES. Miss it and ANOTHER LETTER GRADE GONE

I have taken 2 classes with Dr. Love, MUS225 and MUS226. Both classes have the same structure, with regular readings and reflections and a big project at the end of the semester. The class can be a lot of work, but the material is fun to learn about and Dr. Love is very clear with expectations. She is a fair grader and a really nice person.

Dr. Love is very passionate about music and knows what she's talking about. She can be a tough grader, but if you email or go to her she will help you. 3 short quizzes, 1 paper, and 1 big group project. There are definitely easier gen eds, but I found this course to be interesting.

Don't take Music Industry (MUS225) unless you love writing like 20 papers a semester. 

- 4 700-word essays throughout the semester about class readings
- super long readings + so many of them each week
- lead a 25 minute discussion about one of the readings 
- final project is a website w/ a partner (2000 word essay + 700 wd reflection paper)
extremely harsh grader and not flexible at all

A nice thing about her is that she was very clear on what she expected on assignments through very very detailed rubrics. Not very nice and can sometimes just be condescending but she will help if you go to her. There are a lot of assignments including one huge group project. If you want to get the gen ed credit, take another class.

Took class as a gen-ed, but really enjoyed the teaching style and material. Dr. Love is one of the most caring professors I've had. If you do the assigned readings/listenings and participate then you will do well. Class material is interesting and there's flexibility to explore topics you like.

Really interested class, learned so many cool facts about the music industry and the reasoning behind major music history moments. Tough grader but gives plenty of feedback for the big massive project. Don't be afraid to go to office hours and get help. Discussion heavy with slightly difficult readings but was one of the best parts.

Reading for every class, one essay, and a semester-long project, but not much else work. The project was tough - she is a tough grader and I had trouble figuring out how to make her happy, but she is a great teacher. The class was super interesting and fun to take just to get my art credit out of the way.
